source.title: Blender 2.8 / 2.9 Tutorial #5: Smoothing & Hard Edges (Shading, AutoSmooth, SubSurf, Creases, etc.)
source.creator: BornCG

analysis.study_scope: Hard-surface normal diagnosis, shade smooth vs flat, Auto Smooth, mark sharp, subdivision surface control, edge creases, proximity loops, edge splitting, bevel tool, and weighted bevel modifiers.

episodes.problem: Shade Smooth on low-poly planar surfaces creates severe normal interpolation shadows across 90-degree edges.
episodes.observed_fact: A cube set to Shade Smooth displays dark gradient artifacts across flat faces; Suzanne displays smoothed low-poly facets.
episodes.instructor_claim: Shade Smooth interpolates vertex normals across faces, which fails on hard 90-degree turns.
episodes.interpretation: Shade Smooth alone is insufficient for geometry with distinct sharp boundaries.
episodes.reference_evidence: Smooth shading applied to default cube.
episodes.modeling_decision: Switch back to Shade Flat or utilize angle-based normal overrides.
episodes.visible_action: Right-click context menu -> Shade Smooth, then right-click -> Shade Flat.
episodes.spoken_reason: Smooth shading blends normals across 90-degree face angles, causing unnatural dark shading gradients.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Normals are either fully flat per face or continuously interpolated across adjacent face boundaries.
episodes.failure: Applying Shade Smooth directly to hard-angled primitives without edge limits.
episodes.correction: Revert to Shade Flat or enable normal constraint systems.
episodes.transferable_principle: Vertex normal interpolation across steep angles produces normal shading artifacts on planar surfaces.

episodes.problem: Cylinder walls need smooth shading around the perimeter while maintaining sharp top/bottom cap rims.
episodes.observed_fact: Checking Auto Smooth at 30 degrees keeps cap edges sharp while smoothing side faces.
episodes.instructor_claim: Auto Smooth automatically sharpens edges where adjacent face angles exceed the specified threshold.
episodes.interpretation: Auto Smooth acts as a non-destructive angle-based normal split override.
episodes.reference_evidence: Cylinder mesh with Shade Smooth active.
episodes.modeling_decision: Enable Auto Smooth and adjust the angle threshold below 90 degrees.
episodes.visible_action: Properties -> Object Data Properties -> Normals -> Enable Auto Smooth (set to 30°).
episodes.spoken_reason: Splits vertex normals automatically when adjacent face angles exceed the degree threshold.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Side quads shade smooth together; top and bottom caps maintain sharp split normals.
episodes.failure: Increasing threshold above 90 degrees reinstates unwanted smooth shading across cap edges.
episodes.correction: Keep angle threshold between adjacent face angle (11.25° for 32-sided cylinder) and cap junction angle (90°).
episodes.transferable_principle: Angle-based normal splitting non-destructively preserves sharp boundaries on rotational primitives.

episodes.problem: Auto Smooth angle threshold cannot isolate specific edges when angle thresholds must be set above the feature angle.
episodes.observed_fact: Marking an edge sharp turns it cyan and forces a sharp normal split regardless of the Auto Smooth angle setting.
episodes.instructor_claim: Mark Sharp explicitly forces selected edges to remain sharp when Auto Smooth is enabled.
episodes.interpretation: Sharp edge tags act as manual overrides for the Auto Smooth normal calculation.
episodes.reference_evidence: Cylinder with Auto Smooth set to 94 degrees.
episodes.modeling_decision: Select specific edge loops in Edit Mode and apply Mark Sharp.
episodes.visible_action: Select Edge Loop (Alt+Click) -> Right-Click or Ctrl+E -> Mark Sharp.
episodes.spoken_reason: Explicitly control individual sharp edges when global angle thresholding is insufficient.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Tagged edges highlight cyan in Edit Mode and render with split normals in Object Mode.
episodes.failure: Marking sharp edges without Auto Smooth enabled has no visible shading effect.
episodes.correction: Ensure Auto Smooth option is checked in Object Data Properties.
episodes.transferable_principle: Manual sharp edge tags require an active split-normal evaluation pipeline (such as Auto Smooth) to affect shading.

episodes.problem: Adding a Subdivision Surface modifier to a cylinder distorts the shape into a bulbous mesh with pinched n-gon caps.
episodes.observed_fact: The Catmull-Clark algorithm pulls geometry inward, shrinking the overall volume and collapsing large n-gons.
episodes.instructor_claim: Catmull-Clark subdivides faces and averages positions, causing geometric shrinkage and n-gon distortion.
episodes.interpretation: Subdivision algorithms require boundary edge support to maintain form.
episodes.reference_evidence: Default 32-sided cylinder with Subdivision Surface modifier applied.
episodes.modeling_decision: Implement edge boundary constraints (creases or support loops).
episodes.visible_action: Add Modifier -> Subdivision Surface (Viewport levels set to 2).
episodes.spoken_reason: Unconstrained boundary edges collapse toward centroid averages under Catmull-Clark smoothing.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Mesh shrinks severely at cap boundaries; large n-gon cap vertices distort into severe visual pinches.
episodes.failure: Subdividing raw n-gon cylinder caps without support geometry.
episodes.correction: Constrain edge movement using creases, proximity loops, or split edges.
episodes.transferable_principle: Catmull-Clark subdivision collapses unconstrained sharp angles and distorts large n-gons.

episodes.problem: Subdivision Surface modifier rounds cylinder cap edges that should remain sharp.
episodes.observed_fact: Applying Shift+E and dragging crease factor to 1.0 turns edges magenta and locks their sharpness under Subdiv.
episodes.instructor_claim: Edge Crease tells the Subdivision Surface modifier to refrain from smoothing selected edges.
episodes.interpretation: Creasing provides semi-sharp to infinitely sharp edge retention without altering base topology.
episodes.reference_evidence: Cylinder cap edge loop under Subdiv modifier.
episodes.modeling_decision: Apply Edge Crease (Shift+E) to cap perimeter loops.
episodes.visible_action: Select edge loop -> Shift+E -> Drag mouse or enter 1.0 in operator panel.
episodes.spoken_reason: Weights the edge so the Catmull-Clark algorithm treats it as an un-subdivided boundary.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Selected edges tint magenta; Subdiv modifier maintains an infinitely sharp corner without adding geometry.
episodes.transferable_principle: Crease weighting modifies subdivision evaluation non-destructively without adding extra control geometry.

episodes.problem: Creased edges create infinitely sharp transitions that lack realistic highlight bevels.
episodes.observed_fact: Adding tight loop cuts near outer edges and insetting the top face cap produces a slightly rounded, realistic hard edge.
episodes.instructor_claim: Placing three close proximity loops constrains the Subdiv modifier to create a tight, natural edge radius.
episodes.interpretation: Proximity loops control subdivision curvature localized to the edge region while maintaining quad flow.
episodes.reference_evidence: Cylinder with Subdivision Surface modifier active.
episodes.modeling_decision: Add proximity loops via Loop Cut (Ctrl+R) and Inset Face (I).
episodes.visible_action: Loop Cut -> slide close to top/bottom edges. Select cap face -> Inset Face (I) -> slide slightly inward.
episodes.spoken_reason: Multiple edges placed close together restrict the smoothing algorithm's spatial influence.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Adds quad loops adjacent to the corner; Subdiv creates a tightly controlled, anti-aliased edge highlight.
episodes.failure: Using only two proximity edges across a 90-degree turn leaves slight cap bulge.
episodes.correction: Ensure three adjacent edges (one primary, two support loops on both sides of boundary) define the sharp profile.
episodes.transferable_principle: Geometric proximity loops tightly bound subdivision interpolation, producing realistic highlights.

episodes.problem: Subdivision Surface rounds cap edges when vertices are continuously connected.
episodes.observed_fact: Splitting the cap edge loop (Mesh -> Split -> Selection) detaches cap vertices from side walls, making the cap remain flat under Subdiv.
episodes.instructor_claim: Splitting geometry disconnects vertex points so smoothing cannot interpolate across boundary seams.
episodes.interpretation: Physical topology disconnection prevents Catmull-Clark algorithm from averaging across faces.
episodes.visible_action: Select cap loop -> Mesh -> Split -> Selection.
episodes.spoken_reason: Disconnecting vertices prevents the modifier from calculating smooth interpolations between separated surface patches.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Geometric vertices are duplicated along seam; Subdiv treats caps and walls as isolated surfaces.
episodes.failure: Moving cap face reveals open gap in geometry due to physical disconnection.
episodes.correction: Avoid moving split components, or use non-destructive split modifiers instead.
episodes.transferable_principle: Physical topological disconnections isolate subdivision evaluation between adjacent surface patches.

episodes.problem: Manual geometric edge splitting is destructive, and Edge Split modifier fails when sharp edges branch in multiple directions.
episodes.observed_fact: Adding Edge Split before Subdiv keeps cap sharp; marking vertical wall edges sharp creates severe tearing/gaps in the mesh surface.
episodes.instructor_claim: Edge Split works procedurally along continuous loops, but branching sharp edges cause geometry tears under Subdiv.
episodes.interpretation: Edge Split modifier duplicates vertices, causing Subdiv to shrink open boundary edges away from each other.
episodes.reference_evidence: Cylinder with Edge Split + Subdivision Surface modifiers.
episodes.modeling_decision: Place Edge Split above Subdiv in stack, but avoid branching sharp edge selections.
episodes.visible_action: Add Edge Split Modifier -> Uncheck Edge Angle -> Check Sharp Edges -> Mark vertical edge sharp.
episodes.spoken_reason: Subdiv smooths open boundaries inward; when T-junctions or vertical seams are split, Subdiv pulls the split edges apart, creating holes.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Procedural duplication of boundary vertices causes Catmull-Clark algorithm to treat split edges as open mesh borders.
episodes.failure: Splitting vertical seam edges on a closed cylinder under Subdiv creates visible gaps/tears.
episodes.correction: Limit Edge Split usages to continuous non-branching boundary loops or use support geometry instead.
episodes.transferable_principle: Splitting non-manifold or branching edges prior to subdivision creates surface tearing due to border shrinkage.

episodes.problem: Manual loop cuts require multiple steps to establish consistent support loop distance on hard edges.
episodes.observed_fact: Selecting boundary loops and executing Bevel (Ctrl+B) with 2 segments instantly generates symmetrical support loops.
episodes.instructor_claim: The Bevel tool splits a single edge into multiple parallel edges, generating support loops quickly.
episodes.interpretation: Beveling hard edges with 2 segments creates an immediate support loop structure for Subdiv modeling.
episodes.reference_evidence: Cylinder cap edge loops selected in Edit Mode.
episodes.modeling_decision: Bevel cap edges with 2 segments and small offset.
episodes.visible_action: Ctrl+B -> Drag mouse -> Adjust Width and Set Segments to 2 in operator panel.
episodes.spoken_reason: Splits single boundary edge into three edges (original center plus two outer guard edges).
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Replaces single edge loop with a chamfer/strip of quads; Subdiv creates smooth, realistic edge radius.
episodes.failure: Using 1 bevel segment creates a flat diagonal chamfer that still distorts under Subdiv.
episodes.correction: Set Bevel segments to 2 or more to create proper central and support geometry.
episodes.transferable_principle: Multi-segment edge beveling automatically generates balanced support geometry for subdivision surfaces.

episodes.problem: Adding Bevel modifier after Subdivision Surface results in abnormal mesh ballooning and incorrect bevel placement.
episodes.observed_fact: Dragging the Bevel modifier above Subdivision Surface in the stack restores proper cylinder shape and edge beveling.
episodes.instructor_claim: Modifier stack order is critical: Bevel must generate support loops before Subdivision Surface smooths the mesh.
episodes.interpretation: Top-to-bottom modifier execution dictates that topology generation (Bevel) must precede surface interpolation (Subdiv).
episodes.reference_evidence: Cylinder with Bevel and Subdivision Surface modifiers.
episodes.modeling_decision: Reorder modifier stack so Bevel executes before Subdiv.
episodes.visible_action: Drag Bevel modifier header above Subdivision Surface modifier in the stack.
episodes.spoken_reason: Subdiv needs the bevel geometry to act as support loops during its smoothing pass.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Bevel adds procedural support edges to low-poly mesh first; Subdiv then smooths the resulting quad geometry cleanly.
episodes.failure: Placing Subdiv before Bevel causes Bevel to operate on dense, rounded post-subdivision geometry.
episodes.correction: Ensure topology-generating modifiers (Bevel) precede smoothing modifiers (Subdiv) in stack.
episodes.transferable_principle: Modifiers execute sequentially from top to bottom; structural support generation must precede subdivision smoothing.

episodes.problem: Global Bevel modifier angles bevel all edges indiscriminately across complex objects.
episodes.observed_fact: Setting Bevel Limit Method to Weight and applying Edge Bevel Weight (Ctrl+E) permits variable per-edge beveling.
episodes.instructor_claim: Edge Bevel Weights allow precise per-edge bevel amount control under a single procedural Bevel modifier.
episodes.interpretation: Bevel weights provide selective procedural edge control without modifying underlying mesh connectivity.
episodes.reference_evidence: Cylinder with Bevel Limit Method set to Weight.
episodes.modeling_decision: Set Limit Method to Weight and assign Edge Bevel Weight values to specific edge loops.
episodes.visible_action: Bevel Modifier -> Limit Method -> Weight. In Edit Mode, select edge loop -> Ctrl+E -> Edge Bevel Weight -> Drag to 1.0 or 0.4.
episodes.spoken_reason: Controls exactly which edges receive beveling and allows varying bevel intensity across different parts of the mesh.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Edges marked with bevel weight display blue highlight; Bevel modifier generates procedural chamfers relative to assigned weight values.
episodes.transferable_principle: Weight-limited procedural modifiers grant precise, non-destructive control over individual edge attributes.

33:59 - 36:12 Outro, social media plugs, and general channel promotion.
limitations: Demonstrations focus on basic primitives (cylinders, cubes, monkey head) rather than complete complex production assets.
